history.user: Picked up my first colony of bees this afternoon, a small starter box from a keeper over in Waimanalo. I drove home with it strapped into the back seat and the windows down, humming the whole way. The box, not me.
history.assistant: A humming passenger in the back seat. That is a drive you will remember.

history.user: Moved the frames into the proper hive this morning. I was so nervous that I put my veil on inside out and could not work out why I could see nothing.
history.assistant: Veil on inside out. They were probably as confused as you were.

history.user: Did my first full inspection after work today, Thursday. I finally spotted the queen, on the fourth frame, with a green dot on her back.
history.assistant: A green dot on the fourth frame. Finding her the first time is a small triumph.

history.user: First sting this morning, Saturday, right on the knuckle, because I took a glove off to scratch my nose. My hand looks like a baseball mitt.
history.assistant: One glove off for one itch. The knuckle will remember that longer than you do.

steps.text: Did I say anything to you last Friday, the twenty-fifth?
What about the first few days of September? What were we talking about back then?
When was the very first time I brought up the bees?
